{"decision":"RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL (Anthony, 2026-10-13, thinking out loud after reading about the Azure Maia 300).

HIS WORDS: "We've discussed doing fewer things, but doing those things very well before (for reflow2). ... While this may seem tangential at best, it is the direction that AI is going in. AI models will get better and better and understanding how they will get better is should shape which things that reflow2 starts cutting (via negativa), and keep the things that reflow2 does well. This is because reflow2 is the partnership between AI, human, and a persistent graph (reflow2). The things about maia that I picked up were: Tailored for memory-intensive, emerging AI tasks, including long-context reasoning, latency-sensitive conversational experiences, and multi-step agentic tasks. ... You don't have to look too far to see that which direction AI is going in, so we should start shaping reflow2 appropriately."

THE SIGNAL, as he read it: Microsoft's third-generation inference accelerator (October 2026): 288 GB of HBM4 and 18 TB/s per accelerator, built for memory-intensive inference. Three workloads named: long-context reasoning, latency-sensitive conversation, multi-step agentic tasks.

WHAT IS ALREADY SETTLED, and this idea sits under it: rule:reflow2-is-one-of-three-parts-and-does-not-compete-with-the-others (his direction of 2026-09-02). Its test for any design decision: "is this making one part do another part's job? Build where the three meet." And its explicit limit, in his words then: "I'm not saying let's cut the things that a model can do." Scaffolding a better model needs less of "is allowed to erode on its own; it does not need removing, and removing it would cost today's users to serve a hypothetical." SO THE OPEN PART IS NOT WHETHER TO SHAPE reflow2 toward the seams; it is (1) which things, read against the three named workloads, and (2) whether the hardware signal moves his 09-02 position from "let it erode" to "cut it now". (2) is his to reopen, not the agent's to frame.

READING THE THREE WORKLOADS AGAINST THE THREE PARTS (the agent's derivation, not his):

LONG-CONTEXT REASONING. A model that holds a whole design in context does by itself much of what reflow2's summarising reads do. But context is per session and per model; it ends when the conversation ends, and a different model, a different person or a session a month later starts from nothing. The graph's persistence is across sessions, models and people, which no context window reaches. So long context erodes the SUMMARISING scaffolding and leaves the PERSISTENCE untouched. One more: reflow2's own design is 7,206 records and 53,466 links (2026-10-13), and a model with it all in context still cannot check it without reasoning, and reasoning is what a check must not do (dec:report-dont-judge).

LATENCY-SENSITIVE CONVERSATION. A person talking to a chat will not wait for a design brain. Every reflow2 call on the conversational path has to be fast and its reply small, or the chat stops calling it. This is the one of the three that the design is least ready for: req:time-and-tokens-are-measured-per-task-against-budgets is still proposed, req:context-is-a-modelled-quantity was dropped, and 2026-10-11 measured compare_designs answering 1.4 M characters against a 4,000 budget.

MULTI-STEP AGENTIC TASKS. An agent running many steps needs what reflow2 already holds at the seams: what each step did and why (ChangeEvents), who holds what (claims), what is owed (loop_status), checks that do not reason and cannot be talked round (drift, gates), whose word settles a thing (authority). The more steps an agent runs unattended, the more the record and the authority matter, and the less the workflow-teaching prose does.

IDEAS, none chosen:

TO CUT OR LET ERODE (via negativa):
(a) Skill prose that teaches a model HOW TO THINK (how to brainstorm, how to reason about a cause) as distinct from WHAT TO WRITE AND WHERE. A long-context model holds the method; the record-keeping half is what reflow2 owns. Counter: the root-cause skill's own measured argument is that a skill pulled at the moment of work changes behaviour where a rule read once does not, and on 2026-10-05 three chats did sums in their heads until pointed at calc. Better models still need pointing. Cheap: it is text.
(b) The lessons served on tool descriptions and beside skills, which grow the context cost of every call. Counter: measured in this design, a lesson filed elsewhere did not change the next call. Cheap to trim, and the cost would show as repeated mistakes.
(c) Reads that summarise what a model with the design in context can see for itself (graph_report_markdown, parts of where-am-i). Counter: those reads are for the person as much as the model, and the person never has the design in context. Moderate: removing a tool breaks flo2's catalog and Alex's MCP use (rule: MCP changes are additive).
(d) The 197-tool surface pruned to an orthogonal essential set. Already accepted as intent (dec:idea-prune-the-tool-surface-to-an-orthogonal-essential-set); this idea is a reason to do it, not a new idea. Large: a release per step, and every consumer re-pins.
(e) Vocabulary routing, gap phrasing and find_tools: scaffolding the 09-02 rule says may erode. Counter: a non-technical person on flo2.io is served by the phrasing, not only the model.

TO EMPHASISE (what the seams need more of as models improve):
(f) Persistence across sessions, models and people, said plainly as the thing long context does not give. This is reflow2's oldest claim; the change is to say it where long context is the obvious objection.
(g) Speed and small replies on the conversational path: a latency budget per tool and a reply budget, measured on release builds, with the slow reads kept off the path a chat takes. This promotes the proposed req:time-and-tokens-are-measured-per-task-against-budgets, and would bring back what req:context-is-a-modelled-quantity dropped. Moderate: measurement first, then the cuts it justifies.
(h) The agent-run record: claims, holds, what each step did, what is owed. Mostly built; the emphasis is in the served text and the site.
(i) Checks that do not reason: drift, gates, the rules that refuse. These get MORE valuable as models get more persuasive, because they cannot be talked round. Already built; emphasise, and resist adding judgement to them.
(j) Authority: whose word settles a thing, dated and attributable. An unattended multi-step agent makes this the load-bearing seam. Already built and enforced.

COUNTER-ARGUMENTS TO THE WHOLE FRAME, recorded beside it:
1. Maia is a hardware efficiency signal (tokens per megawatt, bandwidth), not a capability signal. The three workloads are what the chip is sold for, not what models can newly do. Shaping a product to a vendor's marketing line is the kind of move the convexity brainstorm would call concave: small gain if right, hard to undo if the direction turns.
2. "Models will get better" has been true for the whole life of this project, and the partnership framing is asserted, not measured (the rule's own honest hole). A cut made for a hypothetical costs today's users for certain.
3. The 09-02 direction already answers the direction of travel; what this adds is the three named workloads as a lens. The lens is the useful half.

RANKING (a finding, not a decision): (g) is the one that is both cheap to start and the least ready, because measurement comes first and costs no cut. (f), (h), (i) and (j) are emphasis in text, cheapest of all. (a) and (b) are cheap cuts with measured counter-evidence. (c) and (d) are expensive cuts. (e) is the one the 09-02 rule says to leave alone.
